page: Microsoft Azure D96ps_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on an ARM64 processor architecture running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 96 dedicated vCPUs and 384.0 GB of memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per virtual core. It does not include integrated hardware graphics acceleration, operating with zero GPUs.

Storage architecture relies entirely on remote disk attachments. The D96ps_v7 provides no integrated local disk capacity, requiring administrators to provision remote block volumes such as Azure Premium Storage for operating system disks and persistent data workloads. Because of the ARM64 core design, all executing applications must be compatible with 64-bit ARM binaries.

The 96-core ARM topology provides high density and computational efficiency for multi-threaded systems. Workload profiles that align with this resource footprint include enterprise web application tiers, container orchestration nodes, continuous integration compilation engines for ARM software, and distributed caching or database services utilizing remote storage backends.
description: Microsoft Azure D96ps_v7 is a general-purpose ARM64-based virtual machine designed for high-density, multi-threaded computational workloads. Managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs alongside 384.0 GB of system memory, delivering a uniform ratio of 4.0 GB RAM per virtual core. The instance includes no onboard GPU accelerators and features no local ephemeral storage, requiring external network-attached volumes such as Azure Premium Storage for persistent and temporary data handling. The ARM64 architecture delivers balanced computational density and operational efficiency across high-concurrency environments. The D96ps_v7 supports scale-out web application clusters, continuous integration build infrastructure targeted at ARM pipelines, container host clusters, caching layers, and enterprise databases operating over remote storage.
